newsitem.title: USA: Pacific Greystone Q1 shr $0.27 vs $0.13.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Greystone Q1 shr $0.27 vs $0.13.

text.p: (a)Per share data for 1996 was calculated on a pro forma basis assuming the total number of common shares outstanding subsequent to the Company's initial public offering in June 1996 and excluding the preferred dividend requirements.

In commenting on the Company's results, Jack R. Harter, Pacific Greystone's Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, said, "This marks the sixth consecutive quarter of improved year-over-year results. The sharp improvement demonstrates the success of our growth strategy which focuses on maximizing the potential of our existing operations and further expanding into other attractive markets outside of California. Furthermore, the economic conditions in California have continued to improve while our existing operations outside of California have provided profitable growth. At March 31, 1997 the Company's backlog of homes under contract was 814 units, representing aggregate future revenues of $197 million."

At March 31, 1997, the Company's financial position remained strong. The Company's debt to equity ratio was 1.08 to 1.00 at March 31, 1997, while debt to total capital was 52%. In April 1997, the bond rating on the Company's 10 3/4% senior notes was upgraded to Ba3 and B+ by Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's Corporation, respectively.
